chunks: Rijal al-Kashshi: Muhammad ibn Masud, from Ali ibn al-Hasan ibn Fadhal, from al-Abbas ibn A'mir and Ja'far ibn Muhammad ibn Hakim, from Aban ibn Uthman, from Abi Basir who said:

I asked Abu Ja'far (peace be upon him) about the Shahada (witnessing) of a Walad Zina (child born out of wedlock) – is it permissible? He (peace be upon him) said: No. I said: Al-Hakam ibn Utayba claims that it is permissible, so he (peace be upon him) said: O Allah – do not forgive his sin! Allah was not addressing Al-Hakam when He said: 'It is a reminder for you and your people' – let Al-Hakam go to the right and to the left, for by Allah he will not find true knowledge except with the Ahl al-Bayt upon whom Jibrail (peace be upon him) descended.

key_terms.أَهْلُ الْبَيْت: The People of the House (Ahl al-Bayt)
key_terms.الْحُكَمُ بْنُ عُتَيْبَةَ: Al-Hakam ibn Utayba, a contemporary jurist
key_terms.شَهَادَة: Testimony or witnessing in a legal context

ai.seo_question: Is the testimony of a child born out of wedlock valid in Shia jurisprudence?
ai.summary: The Imam (peace be upon him) rules that the testimony of a child born out of wedlock is not permissible. He critiques Al-Hakam ibn Utayba for claiming otherwise, citing the Quranic verse 'It is a reminder for you and your people' to indicate that the verse was not addressed to Al-Hakam, implying his knowledge is insufficient. The Imam concludes that true knowledge is found exclusively in the Ahl al-Bayt.

en.ammaar-muslim: 8. [8/42] Rijal al-Kashshi: Muhammad b. Masud from Ali b. al-Hasan b. Fadhal from al-Abbas b. A’mir and Ja’far b. Muhammad b. Hukaym from Aban b. Uthman from Abi Basir who said:

I asked Aba Ja’far عليه السلام about the Shahada (giving witness) of a Walad Zina (child born out of Nikah) – is it permissible? he عليه السلام said: No. I said: al-Hakam bin Utayba holds it to be permissible, so he عليه السلام said: O Allāh – do not forgive his sin! Allāh was not addressing al-Hakam when He said: “it is a reminder unto you and your Qawm (relations)” [43:44] – let al-Hakam go to the right and to the left for by Allāh he will not find true knowledge except with the Ahl al-Bayt upon whom Jibrail عليه السلام descended.
